subject: License consolidation & renewal roadmap for developer productivity stack
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: License consolidation & renewal roadmap for developer productivity stack

Hi team,

We have three major renewals coming up in Q4 that overlap and give us an opportunity to consolidate pricing / terms: GitHub Enterprise, JetBrains All Products Pack, and our Atlassian suite (Jira + Confluence). I attached a matrix (DevTools_Renewal_Matrix_2026.xlsx) that summarizes current seats, renewal dates, and last-year spend.

Top-level ask: can the procurement + engineering leads agree on a single recommended approach by end of next week so we can ask vendor reps for consolidated quotes? Options I see:
- Keep separate renewals but push for cross-vendor discounts via AWS marketplace (fast)
- Consolidate seat counts, convert inactive seats to Floating or Team licenses (savings)
- Multi-year commit for better unit price but needs executive approval

Please review the matrix and reply with: 1) accurate seat counts for your teams, 2) any hard constraints (compliance/SSO), and 3) priority ranking for vendor negotiation (e.g., push hardest on GitHub or JetBrains).

I'll coordinate vendor outreach once we have the internal counts.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Head of Developer Productivity | Redwood Inference

Attachment: DevTools_Renewal_Matrix_2026.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: License consolidation & renewal roadmap for developer productivity stack

Thanks Dylan — reviewed the matrix. A few quick notes and proposed negotiation priorities: 

Seat counts (validated with team leads):
- GitHub Enterprise (org-wide): 650 active dev seats, ~80 bot/integrations that can be converted to machine users or removed.
- JetBrains All Products Pack: 180 seats (engineering + data platform), ~25 inactive renewals we can reclaim.
- Atlassian (Jira Software + Confluence): Jira 420 users (including contractors), Confluence 380 users. We should aim to move contractors to Team/limited access to reduce cost.

Negotiation priorities (my recommendation):
1) GitHub — highest leverage: large seat count, clear cleanup opportunity, look for enterprise discounts + advanced auditing at no extra charge.
2) Atlassian — push for consolidated Jira+Confluence bundle + commit term.
3) JetBrains — negotiate seat reallocation and a pilot for Floating Licenses (we can cap at 150 concurrent seats).

Constraints:
- All products must continue to support SSO via Okta SAML + SCIM provisioning.
- We cannot accept vendor-hosted code indexing for GitHub without a legal check (privacy).

I can lead vendor outreach for GitHub & Atlassian if Dylan wants me to. Ben, Karthik — can you verify contractor counts and any compliance notes?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, GTM Platforms | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Request for consolidated GitHub Enterprise quote (renewal window Q4)

Hi GitHub team,

We are evaluating options for our Q4 renewal for GitHub Enterprise (Redwood Inference). High level: 650 active developer seats, potential to reduce ~80 seats after cleanup, SSO via Okta, and we need audit log retention of 12 months. Attaching our internal renewal matrix for context.

Can you please:
- Provide a consolidated renewal quote for 650 seats with line items for 1-year and 3-year commitments.
- Show pricing if we convert 80 seats to machine/integration users vs. fully removed.
- Confirm whether advanced audit log access and enterprise SAML features can be included in the quoted price (or as an add-on).
- Share lead time for license changes and any migration steps for seat consolidation.

We'd like to review the initial quote by Friday (2026-08-22). If possible, include a contact for finance/legal to coordinate PO and terms.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: DevTools_Renewal_Matrix_2026.xlsx
From: GitHub Sales <sales@github.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request for consolidated GitHub Enterprise quote (renewal window Q4)

Hi Ben / Marissa / Dylan,

Thanks for the details — attached is a preliminary quote (GitHub_Quote_2026Q3.pdf). Key points: 
- 1-year quote: list price for 650 seats $195,000; with 10% enterprise consolidation discount: $175,500.
- 3-year commit: effective 18% discount with additional price protection; total $480,000 over 3 years.
- Converting 80 seats to machine accounts reduces recurring seat cost by ~$9,600/year (we included that scenario in the quote).
- Advanced audit log export is available as an add-on. We can include 12-month retention in the enterprise bundle for a one-time setup fee (see quote).

Next steps we suggest:
1) Quick 30-minute call to confirm seat mapping and confirm which seats are integrations vs. humans.
2) If you want the 3-year committed option, we can prepare an enterprise agreement and proposed SOW for legal.
3) Finance contact for invoicing / PO: please share your AP email and any vendor registration requirements.

I am copying our Renewals lead (CC'd) and can schedule a call as early as Friday morning.

Best,
Alex Chen
Enterprise Sales, GitHub
sales@github.com
